title: CS weekly digest — a record of every week the digest moved
note: One record per WEEK'S DIGEST that was written or that failed, filed by the mini worker's cs-refresh tick (card GORG-C3, components/cs-metrics/digest.py, wired in platform/workers/mini-worker/cs_adapter.py). THE DIGEST IS WHAT RETIRES MARIA'S FRIDAY GOOGLE SHEET and the Slack screenshots: refunds by reason plus a feedback summary for one complete Monday-Sunday week, counts and theme aggregates only. The doc itself lands on the data plane at platform/data/cs/<run>/digest/<week>.md; this record is the pointer and the facts about it, never a copy of it. IT READS THE DATA PLANE AND NOTHING ELSE - platform/data/cs/<run>/data.json, no database, no credential, no network - which is precisely why the digest needed NO NEW GRANT ROW: the tag counts it renders ride the refresh's own single warehouse pull (components/cs-metrics/source.sql, @tags_weekly / @tags_raw, appended by this card). NO NEW SCHEDULER either (the one-scheduler rule, 2026-08-27): it runs inside the existing 06:25 America/New_York cs-refresh tick, after a successful refresh and BEFORE the change test, so a digest that moved counts as a moved number and rides the same push. UNCHANGED IS NOT AN EVENT: the digest doc carries no wall clock, so identical data re-renders to identical bytes and files nothing - a run of daily ticks over one week produces at most one record per change, not seven. REFUNDS-BY-REASON IS DATA-DRIVEN: `taxonomy_state` reads `pending` until a refund-reason tag reaches gorgias_tickets.tags, and flips to `live` with no code change the week Maria starts applying taxonomy v2 (the checklist the designer approves is new-workflow-design/builds/cs-loop/taxonomy-v2-checklist.md, and her approval IS the taxonomy ruling). Item id = the cs run name; several records exist per run and the LATEST BY `created` WINS - the history is the append-only record, never an edit. AGGREGATES ONLY, inherited from the plane: no email, name, address, order id, ticket id or message text reaches this kind or the doc it points at, and tag values that are email-, phone- or id-shaped are WITHHELD from the digest and counted in `withheld` instead, because a tag is free text an agent typed. ACCEPTANCE IS THE LEAD'S: one real week reconciles against Maria's manual sheet before the sheet retires.

verdict_fields.note: exactly one per record; reserved so a later event on the same kind can join without changing what a digest record means
the cs run name; equals the record's item id and names the plane the digest was computed from

`ok` means the week's digest was rendered and its bytes moved. There is no `skipped` value on purpose: a plane with no complete week yet, a run whose data.json has not been written, or a tree with no digest.py is a LOG LINE and files no record at all - a record is for something that happened.
which wall it hit. One token today because there is one failure mode: the formatter raised something other than its own stated DigestError. A stated absence is never a failure - see `status`.
the failure in words, exception type first. A failed digest NEVER fails the refresh: the numbers are the job, the digest is a rendering of them.
the Monday (YYYY-MM-DD) of the complete week this digest covers - by default the latest complete week on the plane, which is what the tick renders
the Sunday of the same week. Stated rather than derived so a reader never has to know the week convention to read the record.

the warehouse cutoff of the data.json the digest was computed from - the last day both sources were complete. Two digests of the same week under different cutoffs are two different readings, and this is how they are told apart.

THE FIELD TO WATCH. `pending` = no refund-reason tag has reached the warehouse, so the digest renders its stated pending state and Maria's manual sheet is still the record of refund reasons. `live` = taxonomy v2 is being applied and the refunds-by-reason table renders. The flip needs no deploy and no code change; the first `live` record is the start of the one real week the lead reconciles against the sheet.
how many DISTINCT refund-reason tag values appeared in the week. 0 while pending. A number that climbs far past the approved taxonomy means free text is being typed into the tag field.

total refund-reason tag applications in the week. Applications, not tickets: one refund may carry two reasons, which the ledger says is the normal case (size and results complaints arrive fused in one message).
the week's customer-ticket count, from the same weekly grain the cs page reads - the scale every count in the digest is read against

did the run's data.json carry a tag grain at all. false means the run's source.sql predates card GORG-C3's @tags_weekly section, which is a different problem from 'nobody has tagged anything yet' and must not be read as one.

how many tag values were withheld as email-, phone- or id-shaped. Should be 0. Any other number means somebody typed a customer detail into a Gorgias tag - the digest counted it and refused to print it, and the tag wants fixing at the source.
repo-relative path of the digest doc (platform/data/cs/<run>/digest/<week>.md) - a POINTER; the digest's content lives there and is never copied into this record

did the digest's bytes move against what was already on disk. Always true on a filed `ok` record, by construction: an unchanged digest files nothing. Kept as an explicit field so the record states the fact rather than implying it.
was the doc actually written to disk. false with changed=true means a --dry-run: the digest was computed and compared and deliberately not saved.

was the change committed and pushed, by the same push that carried the refreshed numbers. false with changed=true means the data plane did not move overall, or the push failed, or nobody asked for one (a CLI run pushes nothing by design).
